author: Marlon Chaviano
name: figma-plugin
title: Figma plugin
description: A Figma plugin in TypeScript: logic with the typed API, an HTML interface and an esbuild build, ready to load from the desktop app.

writeFiles.content:
<!-- The plugin's UI: runs in an iframe and talks to src/code.ts with postMessage. -->
<style>
  body { font: 12px system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 16px; }
  button { margin-top: 8px; }
</style>
<label>Rectangles <input id="count" type="number" value="3" min="1" /></label>
<button id="create">Create</button>
<script>
  document.getElementById("create").onclick = () => {
    const count = Number(document.getElementById("count").value);
    parent.postMessage({ pluginMessage: { type: "create-rectangles", count } }, "*");
  };
</script>

setupTasks: Figma: in the desktop app, Plugins → Development → Import plugin from manifest, and pick `manifest.json`. When you publish, Figma gives you the final `id`.
instructions:
## How to work here

- `src/code.ts` runs in Figma's sandbox (document access, no DOM); `ui.html` is the interface (DOM, no document access). They talk through `postMessage` / `figma.ui.onmessage`.
- Declare only the permissions you use in `manifest.json` (`networkAccess`, `documentAccess`).
- Close the plugin with `figma.closePlugin()` when its work is done.
- Develop with `npm run watch`. Before finishing: `npm run build`.
